comments.author: David Collett
comments.html:
Nice! Without stories for the depths, how would we find our ways out.

Keep on building. It’s valuable stuff

comments.author: Winston Rowntree
comments.html: I really feel strongly about this one– major kudos for a tremendously well-executed concept. Really great storytelling (so many of these panels are so perfectly executed, especially the last one), not to mention the story being told. You should be proud of the work you produce.

comments.author: Ben
comments.html: That was fantastic. I got excited when I saw you had a new one up, you never disappoint.

comments.author: Said
comments.html: Beautiful.

comments.author: Anarcissie
comments.html: I agree with everything WR said. Great concept, perfect execution.

comments.author: Harry
comments.html: I keep rereading this. You nailed something important here.

comments.author: Kyle Barbour
comments.html: I’m proud to say that I couldn’t agree more with the great Winston Rowntree. Keep up the amazing work.

comments.author: Myrddin Emrys
comments.html: That was excellent. I’m a fluffy story guy who can count the number of days he’s been depressed this year on one hand (I might be able to count the number of days I’ve been depressed for a full day in the last _decade_ on one hand). But I understand the value of art which finds common ground with those in a subterranean mood. That was an excellently executed metaphore.

comments.author: Vlad
comments.html: Thank you

comments.author: Kevin
comments.html:
That’s pretty damn beautiful. I’ll have to re-read it at home so I can really take in the detail, especially the first panel.

Light can only shine in darkness.

comments.author: Beatriz
comments.html: That’s great, man.

comments.author: Rory
comments.html:
Great idea, and really nicely executed. I love the expressions/posture/clothing of the builder, and just the overall thing you’re getting at.

This is easily my favourite thing you’ve done to date, next to the the Broken Hand one.

comments.author: Doyle
comments.html: Wow.

comments.author: Erdosain
comments.html: I too side with WR The Great… it’s really something special. Resonates with something within. What that is, i can’t really tell.

comments.author: cbobgo
comments.html: when I first looked at this on my phone I think I missed that they were calling the balloons stories, or at least I didnt catch the significance. But reading it again now, it really hit me. Great work, keep it up.

comments.author: dolo
comments.html: Hope the balloons don’t stop coming

comments.author: JayJay
comments.html: Very beautiful.

comments.author: Mr. Howl
comments.html: Outstanding work.

comments.author: Mr. Howl
comments.html: Outstanding work. I hope you don’t mind if I feature it here, properly credited of course: idkartbut.tumblr.com

comments.author: Victor Breum
comments.html: Man this is fantastic. I often feel like there should be more art for the mud-people. This affects me so personally, I feel like I’ve been hit. But hit with an uppercut, so that I could reach that handle above me.

comments.author: anon
comments.html: I have to say, I tend to get emotional easy- but I’ve never had my eyes welt up from such a succinct story. I’ll remember this comic for the rest of my days and am so grateful I’ve come across your work in this big ocean of webcomics.

comments.author: Geoff
comments.html: This is the truth. Thanks for making it.

comments.author: Kelly Barnhill
comments.html: This was wonderful. Thank you so much.

comments.author: amy
comments.html: Ecellent.

comments.author: S. Weippert
comments.html: If what you do makes a positive difference in even one person’s life, it is worth doing.

comments.author: Pedes
comments.html:
I’m not sure how to express what this comic makes me feel apart from…

YES.

comments.author: biztheclown
comments.html: Great comic! Bookmarked!

comments.author: Packbat
comments.html:
I saw this this morning, and thought it was amazing. Every time I look at it again, it gets better.

What this says to me: If you find a work of art – be it a story, a game, a piece of music, anything – that doesn’t speak to you, and you think that makes it unworthy, shut the fuck up. Because not every thing is for you. And because sometimes the people that this work is for need it more than you can imagine.

Thank you so much for making this.

comments.author: Kim Wells
comments.html: One of the things I really love about this work is the way you use the power of the medium to your advantage. The short story scenes at the top then build to those long scrolling panels at the bottom, drawing your viewer along on the journey the balloon takes, and then back up with the final panel. It’s just breathtaking. Nicely done.

comments.author: Vertigo Vixen (@BauboGiggles)
comments.html: Thanks for this… It was cross posted on the discussion thread of John Scalzi’s blog (I tweeted it as well btw) as an example of the power of darkness in storytelling… Not everyone trusts, expects or desires sunshine & rainbows & those things don’t reflect everyone’s experiences… Thanks for showing just what that kind of storytelling means to people who need it….

comments.author: ADifferentRandomAsshole
comments.html: Brilliant
